title: Resilient residency-change event API and tamper-evident evidence envelope
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a robust API and delivery envelope for residency-change and retention-related audit events that produces tamper-evident, verifiable evidence bundles suitable for long-term archival and regulatory inspection. This task defines the event schema, signing/envelope rules, delivery semantics (webhook + archive), and integration points with the existing webhook gateway and evidence storage pipeline.

Problem statement:
- Customers require provable records when data residency or retention metadata changes (e.g., user-requested data movement, legal hold toggles, automated retention expirations).
- Current compliance webhooks emit raw events but lack a standardized, signed 'evidence envelope' that bundles payload + provenance metadata + delivery audit trail.
- We must avoid creating additional operational fragility (latency/throughput regressions for the shipper) while meeting region-anchored residency requirements and regulatory retention/immutability expectations.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
1) Define a JSON-based "evidence envelope" schema that contains: event payload, residency assertions, prior-state snapshot (if applicable), event_id (ULID), monotonic sequence metadata, producer identity, and a signature block (JWS compact or detached).
2) Envelope must include a minimal canonicalization ruleset so signatures are deterministic across language SDKs.
3) Delivery semantics: at-least-once webhook delivery with deduplication via event_id + idempotency-key header. Receiver-facing contract in Confluence and webhook gateway changes documented.
4) Server-side archival: every envelope persisted to the region-anchored evidence ledger for retention TTL and export. Envelope stored both as signed blob and as metadata entry for fast search.
5) Provide a lightweight verification library (node + go) that validates envelope signature via public keys discovered from our JWKS endpoint and checks residency assertions against ledger records.
6) Backwards compatibility: gateway must continue emitting legacy events until all major customers migrate; transitional header x-redwood-evidence-version will indicate envelope versus raw payload.
7) End-to-end integration tests and a canary rollout that verifies performance impact under typical load (no more than 10% p50 latency increase for the shipper).

API / Schema highlights:
- top-level fields: envelope_version, event_id, event_type, timestamp, producer, residency: {region, residency_basis}, prior_state_digest, payload (opaque JSON), signature: {alg, jws, signer_id}, provenance: {delivery_attempts, webhook_target, delivered_at}  
- canonicalization: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) v1 subset (strings normalized, ordering defined).
- signatures: JWS using RS256 or ECDSA_P256 with keys in Redwood JWKS. For long-term archival we will also compute a SHA-256 content-hash and include it in the envelope to support future Merkle anchoring.

Delivery / Operational model:
- Webhook gateway will attach x-redwood-envelope-id and x-redwood-evidence-version headers. If an envelope build step fails (KMS unavailable), fallback policy: enqueue event into durable retry queue and emit an unsigned minimal-event with header x-redwood-evidence-fallback=true for audit.
- The shipper will batch envelope archival writes to reduce IOPS; archival must preserve ordering per customer+region.
- On the consumer side, recipients may opt into verifying signatures via our public JWKS. We will publish verification examples and a small reference library.

Security considerations / KMS integration:
- Signing key material managed in KMS/HSM; rotation semantics defined in Confluence. Signer_id references a rotating key alias.
- Security review required for canonicalization + signing code paths to avoid signature malleability.
- If HSM path is unavailable, we will fail closed for primary evidence generation (i.e., keep event in queue). Fallback unsigned emission is opt-in per customer via feature flag.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Synchronous signing increases latency; batching reduces per-event cost but complicates timely proof generation. We decided to sign per-event at producer but allow asynchronous double-anchoring: immediate JWS + background Merkle anchoring job.
- Using JWS makes verification interoperable; adding a content-hash supports future blockchain/Merkle anchoring without changing the envelope contract.

Rollout plan:
1) Design doc & schema review (this ticket). 2) Implement producer-side envelope builder + local unit tests. 3) Integrate with webhook gateway and archival writer (feature-flagged). 4) Publish verification library and Confluence doc. 5) Canary with three customers and internal audit team. 6) Full rollout and deprecation schedule for legacy events.

Links / artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Residency+Evidence+Envelope
- Design PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12845
- Implementation branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tree/feature/evidence-envelope-signing
- Canary dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/Compliance/canary-evidence-envelope
- Related ticket (ledger persistence): ENG-61234

Open questions / next steps:
- Do we require HSM-backed signing for all customers by default or only for enterprise/Private deployments? (security team leaning towards HSM for regulated tiers).
- Define retention policy exposure in API (should we allow customers to receive evidence exports via API or only through compliance exports?).
- Finalize canonicalization subset and publish interop test vectors.

Acceptance checklist (dev):
- [ ] JSON schema committed and published in Confluence
- [ ] Node + Go verification libraries published in internal package registry
- [ ] Gateway and archival integration implemented behind feature flag
- [ ] End-to-end tests with signature verification passing in CI
- [ ] Performance regression < 10% p50 for shipper under test load

QA notes:
- Test vectors include: residency-move, retention-expire, legal-hold-toggle, manual-corrective-move. Each vector must include prior_state_digest case and multi-attempt delivery trace.
